chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, good character (al-khuluq) is a gift that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, grants to His creation. From it is natural disposition (sajjiyyah), and from it is intention (niyyah). So I said, 'Which of the two is superior?' He said: 'The one with the natural disposition is innate and cannot choose otherwise, while the one with intention is patient in obedience with patience; therefore, he is superior of the two.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between natural good character and acquired good character in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the distinction is drawn between innate temperament (sajjiyyah) and deliberate spiritual striving (niyyah), with the latter deemed superior due to the virtue of patience (sabr) in worship. This aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on the merit of effort over mere natural endowment, reflecting the concept of 'fada'il al-a'mal' (excellence of deeds). The hadith underscores that moral excellence is not just a gift but a cultivated state achieved through conscious discipline.
